title: Lesson 5: Giving and Receiving Instructions
summary: Effective teamwork depends on two responsibilities: giving instructions clearly and receiving them attentively — then following through and reporting the outcome.

items.label: Focus
items.body: Clear instructions, active listening, accountability, task execution and professional communication

sections.title: 1. Introduction
paragraphs: Imagine a supervisor tells a therapist: "Please prepare the room for the next client."
The therapist enters the room, arranges the massage bed and leaves.
A few minutes later, the client arrives.
Unfortunately, the towels have not been replaced, the massage oil is almost finished and the room has not been properly checked.
The supervisor becomes frustrated because the room was not fully prepared.
The therapist responds: "But you only told me to prepare the room. You didn't tell me everything I should do."
Now consider another situation.
The supervisor says: "Please prepare Room 2 for the 3 p.m. appointment. Replace the towels, check the massage oil, ensure the room is clean and inform reception when everything is ready."
The therapist listens and responds: "Understood. I'll prepare Room 2 and confirm with reception once everything is ready."
The second situation is more likely to produce the expected result because the instruction is clear, the employee understands what is required and there is a way to confirm completion.
Effective teamwork depends on two responsibilities: giving instructions clearly and receiving them attentively.
At Zura Spa, both responsibilities are essential to maintaining service standards and smooth daily operations.

sections.title: 2. What is an instruction?
paragraphs: An instruction is a direction or explanation given to help someone understand what action is required.
An instruction may be communicated verbally, in writing, through a demonstration or through an approved workplace communication channel.
A good instruction should help the employee understand what must be done, how it should be done and when it should be completed.
list: Preparing treatment rooms.
Attending to clients.
Managing bookings and schedules.
Cleaning and hygiene.
Reporting incidents.
Handling equipment and supplies.
Following service procedures.
Completing administrative responsibilities.
Communicating with colleagues.
Maintaining professional standards.

sections.title: 3. Why giving and receiving instructions correctly matters
1. It improves work quality
paragraphs: Clear instructions help employees understand the expected standard and complete tasks correctly.

sections.title: 2. It prevents delays
paragraphs: Employees spend less time correcting avoidable mistakes or repeating work.

sections.title: 3. It strengthens teamwork
paragraphs: Everyone understands their responsibilities and how their tasks contribute to shared goals.

sections.title: 4. It supports client safety and satisfaction
paragraphs: Accurate instructions reduce the likelihood of service errors and help employees respond appropriately to client needs.

sections.title: 5. It reduces misunderstandings
paragraphs: Employees are less likely to make assumptions about what was requested.

sections.title: 6. It improves accountability
paragraphs: When expectations are clear, employees can take responsibility for completing tasks and reporting difficulties.

sections.title: 4. The responsibility of the person giving instructions
paragraphs: Giving an instruction is not simply telling someone what to do.
The person giving the instruction should communicate in a way that makes the task understandable and achievable.
Key principle: An instruction is not fully effective merely because it has been spoken. The intended message must be understood.

sections.title: Seven principles of giving clear instructions
1. Be specific
paragraphs: Avoid vague statements that leave too much room for interpretation.
Instead of: "Make sure everything is fine."
Say: "Please check that the room is clean, the towels have been replaced and the supplies are ready before the appointment."

sections.title: 2. Explain the expected outcome
paragraphs: Employees should understand what successful completion looks like.
For example: "The room should be clean, fully stocked and ready for the client before 3 p.m."

sections.title: 3. State the deadline
paragraphs: If a task is time-sensitive, communicate when it must be completed.

sections.title: 4. Clarify responsibility
paragraphs: Make it clear who is expected to carry out the task.
Avoid assuming that someone will handle a responsibility simply because several employees are present.

sections.title: 5. Provide necessary information
paragraphs: Employees may need access to supplies, equipment, schedules or procedures to complete an instruction.

sections.title: 6. Use respectful language
paragraphs: Instructions should be firm and clear without insults, threats or unnecessary humiliation.

sections.title: 7. Confirm understanding
paragraphs: For important or complex tasks, ask the employee to summarise the instruction or confirm the next step.

sections.title: 5. The responsibility of the person receiving instructions
paragraphs: Receiving an instruction involves more than saying "okay."
Employees should make a reasonable effort to understand what is required and follow through appropriately.
Key principle: Responsible employees do not merely acknowledge instructions. They understand, execute and communicate the outcome.

sections.title: Seven principles of receiving instructions
list: Pay attention. Avoid unnecessary distractions while instructions are being given.
Listen without unnecessary interruption. Allow the person to explain the task before responding.
Ask questions when something is unclear. Do not guess when an important detail is missing.
Confirm the instruction. Repeat critical details where necessary.
Understand the priority. Determine whether the task is urgent and how it relates to other responsibilities.
Communicate difficulties promptly. If you lack the resources, time or ability to complete the task as expected, inform the appropriate person early.
Report completion accurately. Do not claim that a task is complete when important steps remain unfinished.

sections.title: 6. The difference between acknowledging and understanding an instruction
paragraphs: An employee may say "yes," "okay" or "understood" without actually knowing what to do.
This can create problems.
Acknowledgment is useful, but confirmation is especially important when instructions are complex, urgent or safety-related.
table: "I'll replace the towels and check the supplies."
"I'll contact the client and confirm the new time."
"I'll complete the task and update reception."
"I'll report the issue to the supervisor immediately."

sections.title: 7. The six essential elements of a good instruction

items.label: What?
items.body: What task needs to be completed?

items.label: Who?
items.body: Who is responsible for completing the task?

items.label: When?
items.body: What is the deadline or expected completion time?

items.label: Where?
items.body: Where should the task be carried out?

items.label: How?
items.body: What procedure, standard or method should be followed?

items.label: Confirmation?
items.body: How will completion be verified or communicated?

sections.title: Practical example
paragraphs: "Joy, please prepare Room 1 for the 4 p.m. Swedish Massage appointment. Replace the towels, check the room supplies and confirm that everything is clean. Please inform reception when the room is ready."
This instruction identifies the responsible person, task, location, deadline, expected standard and completion update.

sections.title: 8. Giving instructions respectfully
paragraphs: An employee's position does not justify rude communication.
Supervisors, experienced employees and colleagues assigning authorised tasks should communicate professionally.
Respectful communication encourages employees to seek clarification instead of hiding uncertainty.
table: "Please attend to this task as soon as possible."
"Could you update me on the progress of the task?"
"Let me clarify the part that is unclear."
"Here are the steps and the resources you need."

sections.title: 9. Receiving instructions without unnecessary defensiveness
paragraphs: Employees may sometimes feel frustrated when receiving instructions, especially if they are already busy or believe the task is unfairly assigned.
However, frustration should not automatically lead to disrespect.
Inappropriate response: "Why are you always giving me work? Can't you ask someone else?"
Professional response: "I'm currently preparing another room for a client. Which task should I prioritise?"
The second response communicates a genuine workload concern without attacking the person giving the instruction.
Receiving instructions professionally does not mean employees must comply with unsafe, unlawful, harassing or otherwise improper demands.
Employees should seek clarification, raise concerns and follow appropriate reporting or safety procedures when necessary.

sections.title: 10. What to do when instructions are unclear
paragraphs: Employees should not be afraid to ask reasonable questions.

sections.title: Useful clarification questions
list: "Could you explain what you mean?"
"Which task should I complete first?"
"What time should this be ready?"
"Who should I report to when I'm done?"
"Is there a specific procedure I should follow?"
"Could you demonstrate the expected method?"
"Should I complete this before or after my current assignment?"

sections.title: Zura Spa example — a vague afternoon instruction
paragraphs: A supervisor tells a therapist: "Please handle the afternoon appointments."
The therapist is unsure whether this means preparing the rooms, attending to clients or checking the schedule.
Rather than guessing, she asks: "Please, do you want me to prepare the rooms or attend to the clients assigned for the afternoon?"
The clarification prevents confusion.

sections.title: 11. Handling conflicting instructions
paragraphs: Sometimes employees receive instructions from different people that appear inconsistent.
For example, a receptionist asks a therapist to prepare a room immediately, while a supervisor has already assigned the therapist another urgent responsibility.
The employee should not simply choose whichever instruction she prefers.
Professional response: "I'm currently completing the task assigned by the supervisor. I've also been asked to prepare Room 3. Could we confirm which task should take priority?"
Lesson: Conflicting instructions should be clarified, not turned into arguments or silently ignored.

sections.title: Appropriate steps
list: Identify the conflict.
Explain the existing assignment.
Ask the appropriate supervisor to clarify priorities.
Confirm the final instruction.
Inform affected colleagues of any necessary changes.
Complete the agreed task and provide an update.

sections.title: 12. Reporting progress and completion
paragraphs: Good communication continues after an instruction has been given.
Employees should provide accurate updates when appropriate.
An employee should never report a task as completed when it has not been completed.
Accurate updates help the team make informed decisions.

items.label: A. When a task is completed
items.body: "Room 2 is ready. The towels have been replaced, the supplies checked and reception has been informed."

items.label: B. When a task is delayed
items.body: "The room preparation is taking longer because the required supplies are unavailable. I've informed the supervisor and requested assistance."

items.label: C. When a problem is discovered
items.body: "I noticed that the equipment is not functioning properly. I've stopped using it and reported the issue."

items.label: D. When an instruction cannot be completed
items.body: "I'm unable to complete the task as instructed because the necessary materials are unavailable. Please advise on the next step."

sections.title: 13. A practical method: The DIRECT approach

items.label: D — Define the task
items.body: Explain what needs to be done.

items.label: I — Identify responsibility
items.body: Clarify who will complete the task.

items.label: R — Review requirements
items.body: Identify the expected standard, resources and deadline.

items.label: E — Ensure understanding
items.body: Ask questions and confirm important details.

items.label: C — Carry out the task
items.body: Complete the instruction according to the appropriate procedure.

items.label: T — Tell the outcome
items.body: Report completion, progress or any difficulty.

sections.title: DIRECT example
paragraphs: A supervisor asks an employee to check the treatment rooms before the evening appointments.
The employee confirms which rooms need attention, reviews the required standard, completes the checks and reports any outstanding issues.
This approach helps prevent incomplete work and misunderstandings.

sections.title: Case study A: The incomplete room preparation
paragraphs: A supervisor tells a therapist to prepare a treatment room.
The therapist arranges the massage bed but forgets to replace the towels and check the supplies.
The next client arrives before the room is fully ready.
Expected lesson: Both clear instructions and attentive execution are necessary for successful task completion.
list: Was the instruction sufficiently clear?
What responsibility did the therapist have?
What questions could have prevented the mistake?
How should the supervisor improve future instructions?
How should the employee respond to the error?

sections.title: Case study B: The conflicting assignments
paragraphs: A therapist is preparing a room when the receptionist asks her to assist with another appointment.
The therapist becomes frustrated and says: "Everybody is always giving me work!"
Expected lesson: Conflicting responsibilities should be communicated and prioritised appropriately.
list: What caused the frustration?
What should the employee do when instructions conflict?
Who should clarify priorities?
How can the issue be resolved without conflict?

sections.title: Case study C: The employee who pretends to understand
paragraphs: A new employee receives instructions about a workplace procedure.
She does not understand the process but says: "Yes, I know."
Later, she completes the task incorrectly.
Expected lesson: Asking questions is a professional habit that prevents mistakes and supports learning.
list: Why might the employee have been afraid to ask questions?
What should she have done differently?
How should the person giving the instruction respond?
What can management do to encourage clarification?

sections.title: Case study D: The unreported delay
paragraphs: A receptionist is instructed to confirm several appointments before a particular time.
She encounters a difficulty but does not inform anyone.
The confirmations are not completed, and the team discovers the problem shortly before the appointments.
Expected lesson: Employees must communicate difficulties promptly rather than waiting until problems become urgent.
list: What should the receptionist have done when the difficulty arose?
Why is timely communication important?
How did the lack of an update affect the team?
What would an appropriate progress report sound like?

sections.title: 15. Practical group activity: Instruction relay
paragraphs: Activity duration: 10 minutes.
Purpose: Demonstrate the importance of clarity, confirmation and accurate execution.

Sample instruction: "Please prepare Room 3 for the 5 p.m. Deep Tissue Massage appointment. Replace the towels, check the massage oil, confirm the room is clean and inform reception when everything is ready."
Expected outcome: Participants should understand that effective instructions require clarity, attention, confirmation and follow-through.

sections.title: Instructions
list: Divide participants into groups of three.
Assign one person as the supervisor, one as the employee and one as the observer.
The supervisor gives a workplace instruction.
The employee listens and asks necessary questions.
The employee summarises the instruction.
The observer evaluates whether the task, deadline, responsibility and expected outcome were clear.
Rotate the roles.

sections.title: Discussion
list: Was the instruction specific?
Did the employee ask useful questions?
Were any details missed?
Was the deadline clear?
Was the expected outcome understood?
How would the employee report completion?

sections.title: 16. Interactive assessment
paragraphs: Complete the Lesson 5 Knowledge Check at the bottom of this lesson. Choose an option, give your reason, then submit.
list: What makes a workplace instruction effective? Speaking loudly so the employee obeys / Clearly communicating the task, responsibility, requirements and deadline / Assuming the employee already knows everything
You receive an instruction you do not understand. What should you do? Ask a respectful clarifying question / Pretend to understand and guess / Ignore the instruction
Two people give you conflicting work instructions. What is the best response? Choose whichever task you prefer / Ignore both instructions / Explain the conflict and seek clarification of priorities

A task is delayed because required supplies are unavailable. What should the employee do? Say nothing until the deadline passes / Report the difficulty promptly and seek guidance / Claim the task is complete

Which statement best describes responsible execution of instructions? Understanding the task, completing it appropriately and communicating the outcome / Saying 'okay' even when the task is unclear / Completing only the easiest part of the task

sections.title: 17. Personal assignment
paragraphs: Each employee should answer the following questions in writing.
list: Explain what an instruction means in the workplace.
Identify five characteristics of a clear instruction.
Describe five responsibilities of an employee receiving instructions.
Explain the difference between acknowledging and understanding an instruction.
Describe how you would respond if you received conflicting instructions.
Explain why employees should report difficulties before a deadline is missed.
Describe the DIRECT method in your own words.
Give an example of a poorly communicated instruction and rewrite it clearly.
Identify three personal habits you intend to develop when receiving instructions.

sections.title: 18. Seven-day instruction challenge
table: Ask for clarification when details are missing
Confirm the deadline and expected outcome of a task
Give a colleague a clear and respectful instruction when authorised
Communicate any difficulty before it causes a delay
Reflect on how instruction clarity affected your work

sections.title: 19. Final lesson and takeaway
paragraphs: Giving and receiving instructions correctly is essential to teamwork, service quality and accountability.
At Zura Spa, employees should not assume that an instruction has been understood simply because it has been given.
The person giving an instruction should communicate clearly, respectfully and specifically.
The person receiving it should listen attentively, ask questions when necessary and complete the task responsibly.
Both parties should communicate progress, difficulties and outcomes appropriately.
Next topic: Reporting Issues and Escalating Concerns Appropriately.

remember: Clear instructions create clear expectations. Careful listening creates understanding. Responsible action produces results. At Zura Spa, teamwork improves when employees communicate what needs to be done, understand their responsibilities and follow through with accuracy and accountability. Do not merely hear an instruction—understand it, carry it out and communicate the outcome.
